source: Matei et al. (2026) Ambiguity Detection and Elimination in Automated Executable Process Modeling
finding: Uses model-based diagnosis (gateways as components, minimal hitting sets over conflict sets) inside an LLM loop. GPT-5.1 writes BPMN models from policy text; code compares simulated KPIs; diagnosis points to the gateway and then to the sentence; GPT-5.1 rewrites only that text.
numbers: 100 models generated per policy, 5 KPIs. City 1: after repair more than 90% of regenerated models give the same outcome. City 2: 70% same outcome. Two policies only.
limits: No ground-truth models; only ambiguity that moves the monitored KPIs is found; localisation and repair still rely on LLM prompts; two case studies, no baseline repair method.
agent_relevance: Clearest example found of a code-run MBD step wrapped around an LLM: LLM proposes, code runs and diagnoses, LLM repairs only the located text. Fits G2 (revise from real output).

source: Nakos and Forbus (2024) Interactively Diagnosing Errors in a Semantic Parser
finding: Casts parser debugging as GDE with an assumption-based TMS. The system asks the user natural-language questions as the measurements that split competing minimal diagnoses. Stops when one minimal diagnosis is left.
numbers: Three synthetic ablations of one sentence (Joe ate the apple); all diagnosed after a few questions or none. No user study.
limits: Work in progress; synthetic errors only; limited by the quality of generated paraphrase questions; a model of the parser must be hand-built.
agent_relevance: Shows the GDE loop (pick the most discriminating next probe, ask, update candidates) works when the probe is a question, not a sensor. Template for a code step that picks probes.

source: Orvalho, Kwiatkowska, Janota, Manquinho (2025) Model-Based Diagnosis with Multiple Observations: C Software and Boolean Circuits
finding: CFaults puts all failing tests in one MaxSAT formula and returns only subset-minimal diagnoses. Compared with BugAssist, SNIPER, HSD.
numbers: TCAS: up to 131 failing tests per program; SNIPER hit the 32 GB memory limit on 73% of programs. C-Pack-IPAs: CFaults localises faults in 31% more programs than BugAssist, 36% more than SNIPER, 15% more than HSD; 480 valid (70.38%) on the subset tested. BugAssist non-optimal in 2.4% (TCAS) and 9% (C-Pack-IPAs); SNIPER gave redundant diagnoses in 27% (TCAS) and 55% (C-Pack-IPAs). ISCAS85 circuits: generally slower than HSD, localises faults in 6% fewer circuits. Timeouts 3600 s (C), 1800 s (circuits).
limits: Classical solver study, no LLM. Benchmarks are seeded or student bugs, not production code.
agent_relevance: An exact diagnosis engine can be a code tool. Many failing tests must be handled jointly, not one at a time, or answers become redundant or inconsistent.

source: Orvalho, Janota, Manquinho (2024) CFaults: Model-Based Diagnosis for Fault Localization in C with Multiple Test Cases
finding: Earlier version of the same method. Faster than BugAssist and SNIPER; only subset-minimal diagnoses.
numbers: BugAssist gives a non-optimal diagnosis in almost 6% of C-Pack-IPAs cases in this version. Benchmarks TCAS and C-Pack-IPAs.
limits: Overlaps with c03; no LLM.
agent_relevance: Shows the result held across two paper versions.

source: Feldman, Provan, van Gemund (2010) Approximate Model-Based Diagnosis Using Greedy Stochastic Search (SAFARI)
finding: SAFARI trades guaranteed minimality for speed and returns a diagnosis at any time (anytime). Tested on 74XXX and ISCAS85 circuits against the deterministic CDA and HA.
numbers: Table 4, share of tests solved, weak-fault model: c1908 CDA 0%, HA 6.1%, SAFARI 100%; c432 CDA 74.1%, HA 71.1%, SAFARI 100%; c880 CDA 11.6%, HA 12.4%, SAFARI 100%. SAFARI solves 100% on all 14 circuits and all three fault models.
quote: Safari achieves several orders-of-magnitude speedup over two well-known deterministic algorithms
limits: Diagnosis is not guaranteed minimal; optimality proofs hold for weak-fault and some stuck-at models; circuits only.
agent_relevance: Anytime behaviour matches G6 (never abstain): a code diagnoser can hand back its best candidate set when the budget ends.

source: Yang et al. (2026) SemLoc: Turning Free-Form LLM Reasoning into Executable and Verifiable Semantic Constraints
finding: LLM writes checkable constraints at code anchors; code runs them on passing and failing tests to build a violation spectrum, then verifies a suggested patch by rerunning tests. A test-spectrum cousin of MBD conflict sets.
numbers: SemBugs: 809 real bugs from 750 projects; 4 LLMs. 99.4% of constraints become runtime checks. On tied cases, violations alone rank the fault first in 40.9% vs 2.2% for SBFL and 7.0% for Daikon. 68.4% of top answers carry a test-confirmed patch and 93.6% of those are correct. Acc@1 81.4% vs 50.0% for an LLM that sees only the function.
limits: Fault localisation in code with tests as oracle; not full MBD; the LLM is still the source of the constraints.
agent_relevance: Code-checked verification turns an LLM guess into an answer with a measured reliability. Supports G2 and G3.

source: Yang et al. (2026) SemLoc, comparison and trust results
finding: The structured scaffold did not beat an LLM given the same inputs in one question, but it made answers checkable. Stated LLM confidence was a poor trust signal.
numbers: Acc@1 81.4% (SemLoc) vs 82.0% (LLM given all inputs), no significant difference for any of 4 LLMs. LLMs report confidence of at least 0.9 on 76.2% of answers, yet only 84.1% of those are correct. SBFL fails to rank the fault first in at least 83.8% of bugs.
limits: Same single study; dataset built by the authors.
agent_relevance: The gain from the scaffold was verifiability, not accuracy. Matches G7: judge a scaffold by what it adds at equal inputs.

source: Rafi, Kim, Chen, Wang (2025) LLM4FL: Multi-Agent Fault Localization via Graph-Based Retrieval and Reflexion
finding: Three LLM agents with graph retrieval and reflexion localise faults in Java. Prompt-chaining order changed Top-1 by up to 22%.
numbers: Defects4J, 675 faults. Top-1: LLM4FL 326, AutoFL 275, SoapFL/AgentFL 311, DeepFL 257, Grace 298, Ochiai 121.
limits: One benchmark, likely training-data contamination; gain over SoapFL is 4.82%.
agent_relevance: Order of prompts alone moved results by up to 22%; scaffold detail matters and must be measured.

source: Xu et al. (2025) Exploring the Potential and Limitations of LLMs for Novice Program Fault Localization
finding: 13 LLMs on Codeflaws, Condefects and a new leak-free set (BugT). Reasoning models (o3, DeepSeek-R1) need little prompt engineering; GPT-4 needs careful prompts. Accuracy falls as difficulty rises. Over-reasoning hurts clarity.
numbers: Top-1 fault counts, Condefects: o3 312, GPT-4 200, GPT-3.5 148. BugT: o3 289, DeepSeek-R1 248, GPT-4 192. SBFL baselines far lower. Dataset sizes not recorded.
limits: Table text was garbled in extraction, so some cells are uncertain; novice student programs.
agent_relevance: Reasoning models removed most prompt sensitivity; a diagnosis scaffold must be tested against a reasoning-model baseline.

source: Braitsch et al. (2026) Information-seeking failures of large language models in agentic clinical reasoning (OncoRounds)
finding: Models must request data over 3 rounds before committing. The core failure is choosing what to look at next, the step GDE automates with a probe-selection rule.
numbers: 32 frontier models, 20 cases, 1,896 completed runs. Best overall accuracy 68%. Information utilisation predicts accuracy (R = 0.69, P < 0.001) but falls from 57% to 26% in the final round.
limits: Hematologic oncology; cases written by one clinician; not a device-fault task.
agent_relevance: Strong evidence that LLMs under-probe. A code step that ranks next tests by information gain could fix a measured weakness.

source: Braitsch et al. (2026) OncoRounds, reasoning quality versus accuracy
finding: Written reasoning looked good but did not predict correctness. Dominant errors: search satisficing, anchoring, premature closure.
numbers: 91% of reasoning traces above the rubric threshold, yet decorrelated from accuracy.
limits: Same study.
agent_relevance: Do not trust the model's explanation as a diagnosis check (G2, G5); use code checks.

source: Kang, Chen, Yoo, Lou (2023) Explainable Automated Debugging via LLM-driven Scientific Debugging (AutoSD)
finding: Hypothesis, experiment in a real debugger, conclusion loop. Real execution results matter: when the LLM imagined the debugger output, results got worse.
numbers: Defects4J v1.2: LLM-Base 87, AutoSD 76 plausible patches; v2.0: 110 vs 113 (Recoder 24 and 11, InCoder 41 and 28). With real execution 73% of runs plausible vs 63% when the debugger was ablated. Human study: 20 participants (6 professionals); 70% wanted explanations, 55% satisfied.
limits: ChatGPT default model; patch counts are plausible, not all verified correct; no formal system model.
agent_relevance: Strong support for G2: observations must come from code, not from the model's simulation of them.

source: Olausson et al. (2024) Is Self-Repair a Silver Bullet for Code Generation?
finding: Self-repair is held back by the quality of the model's own diagnosis of its code. Stronger feedback helps; human diagnosis helps most.
numbers: GPT-4 repair success with GPT-4 feedback 33.30% vs human feedback 52.60% overall (introductory 42.64% vs 62.21%; interview 19.33% vs 45.67%; competition 3.67% vs 14.67%). 16 participants wrote feedback on 40 failing programs. Gains often modest once cost is counted.
limits: HumanEval and APPS; small human study.
agent_relevance: The diagnosis step is the bottleneck, not the repair step. A code-run diagnoser could supply better feedback than the model can write about itself.

source: Zhong, Wang, Shang (2024) Debug like a Human: LDB
finding: Splits the program into basic blocks, records variable values after each block, and has the LLM check each block against the task. A runtime-trace version of checking components against a model.
numbers: Improves baselines by up to 9.8% on HumanEval, MBPP and TransCoder.
limits: Code generation benchmarks; no explicit fault model.
agent_relevance: Component-by-component checking with real traces is close to the observe-then-localise cycle of MBD.

source: Chen et al. (2024) Teaching Large Language Models to Self-Debug
finding: Few-shot self-debug with execution feedback or self-explanation.
numbers: Spider: +2 to 3%, +9% on the hardest level; TransCoder and MBPP: up to +12%.
limits: Gains vary by benchmark.
agent_relevance: Execution output is the observation; explanation alone helps when tests are missing.

source: Englhardt et al. (2023) Exploring and Characterizing LLMs for Embedded System Development and Debugging
finding: Hardware-in-the-loop test of GPT-3.5, GPT-4, PaLM 2 on embedded tasks.
numbers: N=450 experiments; GPT-4 made functional I2C interfaces in 66% of N=50 trials; perfect code on the most complex tasks 14% of the time. 15 users: LoRa sensor success 25% to 100% with the workflow.
limits: Generation more than diagnosis; small user study.
agent_relevance: A real physical check gives a trustworthy grader for hardware tasks.

source: Moddemann et al. (2023) Discret2Di: Deep Learning Based Discretization for Model-Based Diagnosis
finding: Learns logic rules for consistency-based diagnosis from time series; targets weak-fault models because faulty data is scarce.
numbers: Tested on two artificial and two real data sets and a three-tank simulation; no headline figure recorded.
limits: Not an LLM method; the model is learned from data.
agent_relevance: The system model can be learned instead of hand-written, a route to MBD without a modeller.

source: Steude et al. (2023) Diagnosis Driven Anomaly Detection for CPS
finding: A deep anomaly detector produces the symptom inputs that consistency-based diagnosis needs.
numbers: Composite F1 0.52 on SWaT, among the best of models compared; subsystem-level evaluation on a simulated set only.
limits: No labelled symptoms in public data, so subsystem tests are simulated.
agent_relevance: Detection and diagnosis must be built together; the diagnoser is only as good as its symptoms.

source: Bertossi (2026) Reconciling Consistency-Based Diagnosis with Actual-Causality-Based Explanations
finding: Proves links between minimal diagnoses and actual causes: an abnormality atom is an actual cause iff it belongs to a minimal diagnosis (propositional case).
numbers: Theoretical; no experiments.
limits: Propositional only.
agent_relevance: Gives a formal base for explaining a diagnosis as a cause, useful for explainable repair reports.

source: Kumar et al. (2025) Building Domain-Specific Small Language Models via Guided Data Generation (DiagnosticSLM)
finding: 3B model tuned for automotive diagnosis; four new benchmarks. No system model or solver is used.
numbers: DiagnosticMCQ 876 questions: DiagnosticSLM 45.32% (397/876) vs Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct 36.53%, Gemma-2 9B 45.21%; base 3B 27.05%. Authors claim up to 25% gain over 2-9B open models.
limits: Multiple-choice knowledge, not fault search; benchmarks by the authors.
agent_relevance: Knowledge-style tests are weak proxies for diagnosis ability.

source: Yang et al. (2025) PHM-Bench
finding: Framework to evaluate large models on condition monitoring, fault diagnosis, remaining-life prediction and maintenance tasks.
numbers: No figures recorded; I read only the abstract and introduction.
limits: Skim only.
agent_relevance: A possible test-set source; not used for claims.

source: Zhang et al. (2024) AutoCodeRover
finding: Agent using code search and spectrum-based fault localization (search listing only).
numbers: 19% on SWE-bench-lite (listing gist).
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Spectrum ranking is already used inside an agent loop.

source: Automated Repair of C Programs Using LLMs (2025)
finding: Loop of SBFL, runtime feedback and chain of thought (listing gist).
numbers: 44.93% accuracy on Codeflaws.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Another example of fault-ranking code plus an LLM.

source: FuseFL (2024) Demystifying Faulty Code with LLM
finding: Combines SBFL ranks, test results and code descriptions in one prompt (listing gist).
numbers: No figures seen.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Code ranks fed to the model as evidence.

source: SiblingRepair (2026)
finding: Finds sibling code near SBFL spots and repairs multi-hunk faults (listing gist).
numbers: No figures seen.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Same pattern.

source: LogEval (2024) Benchmark Suite for LLMs in Log Analysis
finding: Benchmark with log parsing, anomaly detection and fault diagnosis tasks (listing gist).
numbers: No figures seen.

finding: Ensembles quantify uncertainty to cut false alarms in data-driven diagnosis (listing gist).
numbers: No figures seen.

source: Integrated Novelty Detection Systems (2026)
finding: Combines probabilistic fault detection with consistency-based diagnosis to find blocked rain gauges (listing gist).
numbers: No figures seen.
